findings.title: font='sans-serif' (or any hyphenated family name) crashes hyp.plot with a cryptic fontconfig ParseException instead of the documented helpful error
findings.description: fonts.py resolve_font() line 222 calls FontProperties(family=font) with a single bare string. When family is the ONLY argument and the string contains '-', matplotlib treats it as a fontconfig pattern and its parser raises ValueError wrapping a pyparsing ParseException -- OUTSIDE resolve_font's try block (which only wraps findfont), so the crafted 'not a recognized installed font family... Pass a valid installed family name...' message documented in the docstring is never produced. 'sans-serif' is matplotlib's canonical generic family (rcParams default) and the most obvious value a user would pass; 'Sans-Serif' fails identically. Non-hyphenated unknown names (e.g. 'nosuchfontxyz') correctly produce the good ValueError. Verified fix: pass the family as a list -- FontProperties(family=[font]) resolves 'sans-serif' fine (findfont then succeeds).
findings.repro:
cd /tmp && env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot(np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(10,3)), font='sans-serif', reduce=None, show=False)
"
findings.expected: Either the font resolves (matplotlib accepts 'sans-serif' everywhere else, e.g. FontProperties(family=['sans-serif'])) or the documented ValueError: "font='sans-serif' is not a recognized installed font family... Pass a valid installed family name, a path to a .ttf/.otf/.ttc file, or a ... FontProperties instance."
findings.actual:
ValueError: 
sans-serif
    ^
ParseException: Expected end of text, found '-'  (at char 4), (line:1, col:5)
  [raised from matplotlib/_fontconfig_pattern.py:88 parse_fontconfig_pattern, via FontProperties(family=font) at hypertools/plot/fonts.py:222] | RUN-2 reverified verbatim: ValueError : \nsans-serif\n    ^\nParseException: Expected end of text, found '-'  (at char 4), (line:1, col:5). Crash occurs at FontProperties(family='sans-serif') construction, BEFORE resolve_font's guarded findfont try/except, so the documented helpful ValueError never fires.
docs_impact: hypertools/plot/fonts.py (resolve_font docstring promises ValueError 'listing what was tried')

findings.title: `import hypertools.plot.colors` / `.fonts` / `.interactive` / `.multiindex` as-import fails: plot() function shadows the plot subpackage, with a cryptic ImportError
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py binds the plot() FUNCTION to the attribute hypertools.plot (type(hypertools.plot) is function, __name__='plot'), shadowing the hypertools.plot subpackage attribute. Consequently the natural spelling `import hypertools.plot.interactive as interactive` fails with "ImportError: cannot import name 'interactive' from 'plot' (unknown location)" -- a message that names neither hypertools nor the real cause. `from hypertools.plot import interactive` works (Python's from-import falls back to sys.modules). Affects every public helper module in this unit. Longstanding hypertools design (hyp.plot() is the API), but the error deserves a mention in docs and the from-import spelling should be the documented one.
findings.expected: Either the import works, or documentation states that plot submodules must be imported via `from hypertools.plot import <mod>`.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'interactive' from 'plot' (unknown location)   [also: print(type(hypertools.plot)) -> <class 'function'>; sys.modules['hypertools.plot'] is the real module] | RUN-2: 'import hypertools.plot.fonts as m' -> ImportError: cannot import name 'fonts' from 'plot' (unknown location); plain 'import hypertools.plot.fonts' succeeds but 'hypertools.plot.fonts' attribute access -> AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'fonts'; 'from hypertools.plot import fonts' works. Root cause verified: hypertools/__init__.py line 4 'from .plot.plot import plot' rebinds the attribute.
docs_impact: docs (any page telling users to import plot submodules)

findings.title: mat2colors: a single NaN silently collapses the entire 1D continuous color mapping (min and max get identical colors); NaN rows in 2D silently become uniform blends
findings.description: 1D path: edges = np.linspace(np.min(vals), np.max(vals), n_bins+1) becomes all-NaN when any value is NaN, so np.digitize puts every finite value in bin 0 -- ALL points get (nearly) the same color with no warning or error. Demonstrated: mat2colors([0.0, np.nan, 1.0]) colors 0.0 and 1.0 identically. 2D path: a NaN row's sum is NaN, the row_sums>0 test is False, and the row silently receives uniform weights -- indistinguishable from a genuine [0.5,0.5] mixture row. NaNs are routine in scientific data (dropped trials, missing observations); a silent total collapse of the hue mapping is wrong-results behavior, mitigated only by the fact that plot(hue=...) users would usually notice a monochrome plot. Suggest nanmin/nanmax + a UserWarning (or an explicit error) when NaNs are present. RUN-2 END-TO-END CONFIRMATION (2026-07-12): hyp.plot(traj, '-', hue=t_with_one_NaN, palette='viridis') renders the ENTIRE 300-point trajectory in one uniform yellow (viridis top color) -- the time gradient is completely destroyed by a single NaN, silently (no warning, no error; see w4_nan_hue.png vs w2b_continuous_hue_viridis.png). Mechanism detail: with NaN edges, np.digitize returns len(edges) for every finite value -> clip -> ALL finite values get pal[99] (top color) and the NaN entry gets pal[0]. Upgraded minor -> major: clearly-wrong visual through the public hue= path on reasonable input.
findings.repro:
/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np
from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors
print(np.round(mat2colors([0.0, np.nan, 1.0]), 4).tolist())
print(np.round(mat2colors(np.array([[0.5,0.5],[np.nan,0.5]])), 4).tolist())
"
findings.expected: Finite values keep their full-range mapping (nanmin/nanmax) with NaN entries flagged (warning + sentinel color), or a clear error naming the NaN.

findings.title: vals2colors/vals2bins (legacy, re-exported as part of the public coloring surface): color coverage depends on the ABSOLUTE data range; small-range data collapses to a single color
findings.description: Both helpers bin with np.linspace(np.min(vals), np.max(vals)+1, res+1) -- the '+1' makes the covered fraction of the colormap equal range/(range+1). Data in [0,1] uses only ranks 0..50 of a 100-color map; data in [0,0.001] maps everything to rank 0 (one color); data in [0,100] spans 0..99. mat2colors' continuous path (full span regardless of scale) and vals2colors therefore produce visibly different colorings for the same values, despite colors.py's comment calling this module 'the single coloring surface'. This is faithful legacy hypertools-0.x behavior, but for 1.0 either the semantics should be documented on the docstring ('coverage depends on data range') or the binning fixed to match mat2colors.
findings.repro:
/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, seaborn as sns
from hypertools.plot.colors import vals2colors, vals2bins
pal = np.array(sns.color_palette('viridis', 100))
for lo, hi in [(0,1),(0,0.001),(0,100)]:
    cols = vals2colors(list(np.linspace(lo,hi,5)), cmap='viridis')
    print((lo,hi), [int(np.argmin(np.linalg.norm(pal-np.array(c),axis=1))) for c in cols])
"
findings.expected: Same relative values -> same relative colors regardless of absolute scale (as mat2colors does: ranks [0,25,50,75,99]).

findings.title: mat2colors docstring omits the signed-matrix per-row-shift semantics and their consequences (2-column signed rows can only be pure vertex colors; one negative row changes the colors of valid non-negative rows)
findings.description: The signed-input handling (per-row min-shift when the GLOBAL min is negative) is documented only in an inline comment, not in the docstring a user sees via help(). Consequences verified by real runs: (a) every signed 2-column row shifts to [0,x] or [x,0], so it maps to a PURE component color or the uniform blend -- never an intermediate blend; rows [-1,1] and [-100,100] get identical colors (within-row pattern only, cross-row magnitude discarded); (b) because the trigger is the global min but the shift is per-row, adding one signed row changes the color of an unrelated valid proportion row: [0.25,0.75] alone -> 0.25*c0+0.75*c1 blend, but [[-1,1],[0.25,0.75]] -> the [0.25,0.75] row becomes [0,0.5] -> PURE c1. These may be acceptable design choices for arbitrary embeddings (colors reflect within-row direction), but they are invisible to users reading the docstring, which only describes the non-negative mixture-proportion case.
findings.repro:
/Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np
from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors
print(mat2colors(np.array([[0.25, 0.75]])))
print(mat2colors(np.array([[-1.0, 1.0], [0.25, 0.75]]))[1])
print(mat2colors(np.array([[-1.0, 1.0], [-100.0, 100.0]])))
"
findings.expected: Docstring documents: negative inputs are per-row min-shifted before normalizing; mixing signed and non-negative rows changes the non-negative rows' colors; signed k=2 matrices yield only vertex/uniform colors.
findings.actual: [0.25,0.75] alone -> [0.47  0.714 0.73] (correct blend); with a signed row present -> [0.34 0.8288 0.86] (pure c1); [[-1,1],[-100,100]] -> identical rows [[0.34 0.8288 0.86],[0.34 0.8288 0.86]]. Docstring says only: 'Rows are normalized to sum to 1 and each sample's color is the proportion-weighted blend'.

findings.title: CJK auto-font picks Hiragino Sans W0 (ultra-light weight) on macOS -- Japanese text renders hairline-thin next to regular-weight ASCII
findings.description: _ordered_font_entries() sorts each preferred family's files 'by filename for determinism' (fonts.py line 132). On macOS the Hiragino Sans family ships as ~10 .ttc files whose names sort W0 < W1 < ... < W9, so the FIRST covering candidate is /System/Library/Fonts/ヒラギノ角ゴシック W0.ttc -- the ultra-light weight. In w3_cjk_labels.png the title and point labels are real glyphs (no tofu -- the feature works) but visibly hairline compared to the DejaVu-rendered ASCII of other plots (compare w2_multiindex.png's title). Deterministic but weight-naive. Suggest preferring a regular weight (e.g. sort key that ranks 'W3'/'W4'/'Regular' first, or resolve the FAMILY name via findfont and let matplotlib pick the normal weight). RUN-2: resolved file is /System/Library/Fonts/HiraginoKakuGothic(W0).ttc (ttflist name 'Hiragino Sans', thinnest of W0-W9; _ordered_font_entries sorts each preferred family's files by FILENAME so W0 always wins on stock macOS). End-to-end hyp.plot with CJK labels renders the WHOLE plot's text (including the ASCII title) in this hairline weight -- see f4_cjk_labels_endtoend.png vs any non-CJK plot title. Suggested fix: sort candidate files by |weight-400| (entry.weight) before filename.

findings.title: hyp.plot(MultiIndex df, linestyles=[...]) emits one matplotlib 'linestyle is redundantly defined' UserWarning per trace
findings.description: The MultiIndex linestyles feature passes both a fmt string ('-') and a linestyle= kwarg to ax.plot for every trace, so matplotlib warns 'linestyle is redundantly defined by the linestyle keyword argument and the fmt string "-" (-> linestyle="-"). The keyword argument will take precedence.' once per trace (6 warnings for a 6-leaf frame; large frames produce dozens). The rendered output is correct (kwarg wins, which is what multiindex intends; w8_multiindex_linestyles.png shows solid A / dashed B properly). Plain hyp.plot(dfm) without linestyles= emits no warnings. Fix: drop the linestyle character from fmt (or don't pass fmt) when a per-trace linestyle kwarg is set.

findings.title: Default 'hls' palette is circular: continuous-hue minimum and maximum values are visually indistinguishable (through hyp.plot's default)
findings.description: mat2colors' 1D continuous path (and hyp.plot's hue= with the default palette='hls') maps values through seaborn's 'hls' palette, which is a CIRCULAR hue wheel: bin 0 and bin 99 are both red ([0.86,0.3712,0.34] vs [0.86,0.34,0.34], max channel diff 0.0312). A scientist coloring a trajectory by time cannot tell the start from the end under the default settings; the colorbar reproduces the same circular mapping so values can be read back, but the perceptual ordering is broken at the wrap point. viridis/other sequential palettes behave correctly (contrast PNGs).

findings.title: fonts._iter_texts silently skips pandas Series (and dict): CJK hue passed as a Series renders as tofu end-to-end while the identical list works
findings.description: _iter_texts handles str/ndarray/list/tuple/None only. A pandas Series (the natural df['condition'] workflow) or dict is silently skipped, so find_covering_font returns None and no font override is applied. End-to-end: hyp.plot(data, '.', hue=pd.Series(CJK labels), legend=True) draws the legend with the default font -> 30 'Glyph ... missing from font(s) Arial' warnings and tofu boxes in the legend; the identical call with hue=list(...) produces 0 warnings and correct glyphs. plot()'s hue docstring says 'list or numpy array', so Series is technically undocumented -- but hue grouping itself accepts the Series fine (colors/legend labels work), making the font gap a silent inconsistency. Suggested fix: add Series/Index (e.g. via hasattr(obj, 'tolist') or pandas isinstance) to _iter_texts.
